description: Mailchimp sync state recorded on each product. Fields land under $app.mailchimp.* and are written only by functions/lib/sync-state.ts. Outbound only — Mailchimp has no product webhooks, so there is no last_webhook_at here. NOTE: resync/backfill and the saved 'errors' list tab both query sync_status, and that query is a collection scan — Swell has no index declaration yet (developers.swell.is lists 'Custom indexes — Coming soon'). Keep batch sizes small until it ships.

sync_status.label: Mailchimp sync status
sync_status.description: pending: queued, or submitted in a batch that has not finished. synced: accepted by Mailchimp. error: last push failed, see last_error. skipped: Mailchimp will not accept the product and retrying cannot help. canceled: the product was deleted from the Mailchimp store.

remote_key.description: Idempotency key sent to Mailchimp on every outbound call. Always the Swell product id, used verbatim as the Mailchimp product id, which is what makes a repeated push an update rather than a duplicate. Also the 'has this ever been pushed?' flag. Cart and order lines reference the same id, so it must never be derived from the slug or SKU.

remote_id.description: Mailchimp's own id for the product. Mailchimp echoes back the id we supplied, so for this app it is always equal to remote_key; it is kept because the fleet's shared push code reads it and because a mismatch is a useful alarm.

batch_id.description: Id of the Mailchimp batch submission that queued this product, stamped alongside sync_status 'pending' when a batch backfill submits it. Load-bearing for settlement: polling a batch settles only the records stamped with that batch's id, so a poll of one batch can never mis-mark records another batch still has in flight.

variant_count.description: How many variants were included in the last push. Mailchimp requires at least one variant per product, so a product with no Swell variants is pushed with a single default variant whose id is the product id — in that case this reads 1.

last_synced_at.description: When the product was last accepted by Mailchimp.

last_error.description: Message from the most recent failed push, truncated to 500 characters. Cleared on the next success.

resync_requested.description: Set from the dashboard to force a re-push on save. The product.updated handler reacts to it and clears it once the push completes. This is the merchant's manual re-sync button, with no UI code.
